name: Hollow Cathedral

detectability.signature: Massive gravitational lensing ring surrounding a lightless core, with spiraling accretion bands that resemble the vaulted arches of a ruined nave

proximity: Navigation systems suffer progressive drift toward the event horizon
Hull stress sensors trigger under tidal gradient forces
Chronometers desynchronize by 0.3 seconds per hour relative to external observers
contact: Structural failure of unshielded vessels within the accretion disc
Complete navigational blackout as sensor arrays are overwhelmed by radiation
Time dilation reaches a factor of 4:1 at the innermost stable orbit
prolonged_exposure: Irreversible spaghettification beyond the tidal radius
Accumulated radiation dose exceeds lethal thresholds within six standard hours
Psychological deterioration reported by crews stationed at observation distance for more than thirty days

age: Approximately 2.1 billion years, collapsed from a massive O-type progenitor star
phenomena: Photon sphere generates a luminous halo that shifts through ultraviolet and X-ray spectra in a slow, repeating cadence
Relativistic jets extend 0.8 light-years above and below the orbital plane, periodically brightening when captured matter surges
Gravitational lensing produces mirrored ghost-images of distant star systems, some showing light centuries old
A faint harmonic vibration registers on gravimetric sensors, earning the anomaly its name from early explorers who compared it to organ music in an empty church
hazards: Tidal forces capable of shearing capital-class vessels at distances under 0.1 AU
Intense ionizing radiation from the accretion disc
Gravitational capture trajectories that require extreme delta-v to escape once entered
opportunities: The photon sphere offers unparalleled gravitational lensing for deep-universe observation
Relativistic slingshot maneuvers around the ergosphere can accelerate vessels to near-light speeds
Exotic particles harvested from the jet boundaries have theoretical applications in energy generation
known_incidents: The research corvette Vow of Silence was lost with all hands in 3187 after a navigation miscalculation brought it within the tidal disruption radius during a lensing survey mission
A pilgrim flotilla from the Heliarchs of Solace attempted to orbit the photon sphere in 3204, believing the gravitational harmonics to be a divine signal; seven of twelve ships were recovered
description: Hollow Cathedral presents itself as an absence framed by light. At its heart lies a stellar-mass black hole of roughly eleven solar masses, its event horizon a perfect sphere of nothing around which the universe bends and distorts. The accretion disc fans outward in luminous bands of superheated plasma, their arcing geometry so regular that early cartographers described the structure as resembling the ribbed vaulting of some immense, roofless cathedral.

The anomaly's gravitational influence dominates local space for nearly a third of an astronomical unit. Ships that stray within the outer approach markers experience progressive navigational drift, their course vectors subtly but relentlessly curving toward the center. The photon sphere produces a shimmering ring of trapped light that pulses in slow, rhythmic intervals, and gravimetric sensors detect a low-frequency oscillation that crews have likened to the resonance of a vast, hollow space.

Hollow Cathedral has been a fixture of navigational charts since its discovery in 2941, though the surrounding region had been marked as a shipping hazard for centuries before that. It serves as both a waypoint and a warning. Academic expeditions have used its lensing properties to observe galaxies otherwise hidden behind the galactic core, and military theorists have studied its relativistic jets as models for directed-energy weapon research.

Today, a permanent observation platform maintains position at a safe distance of 1.2 AU, staffed by a rotating crew of astrophysicists and navigational surveyors. Recent measurements suggest the accretion rate has increased by a fraction of a percent over the last decade, possibly due to a rogue gas cloud drifting into the capture zone. Whether this heralds a period of heightened jet activity remains an open and somewhat anxious question among the station's residents.
